title: Two little blocks in a tower is the fifteen-month stack
summary: By about 15 months, most children stack at least two small objects, such as blocks, the U.S. CDC says.
body: Stacking at least two small objects, like blocks, is the cognitive line the CDC prints for 15 months. Most, there, means 75 percent or more of children by the age on the sheet. CDC says those Act Early materials are not a substitute for a validated screening instrument. A parenting tip about knocking a tower over is an activity idea, not the milestone itself. The milestone is the tower of two or more. Another country's chart may skip blocks entirely, and nothing here grades one toddler.
